theorem_title: The two encodings of the forbidden configuration agree
natural_language_statement:
For a finite subset $A$ of an additive abelian group, $A$ has a cube exactly when some `config x y z` is a subset of $A$.

The two aren't definitionally equal, because the `Finset` collapses duplicates (at $x = y = z = 1$ modulo 16 it has three elements). They still agree, since being a subset of a `Finset` literal is the conjunction of the memberships.
source: Jason Long and Adam Zsolt Wagner, "The largest projective cube-free subsets of Z_{2^n}", arXiv:1810.01225, https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.01225, the definition of a cube in Section 1; the two encodings are a formalization choice rather than something the paper states
